records.researcher_notes: PJM's first-cycle queue lists request C01-2036: 1150 MW of natural gas generation in Putnam County, Illinois, from Marquis Solar LLC. It was filed on April 27, 2026, connects at the Crescent Ridge to Corbin 138 kV line, and asks to be in service by June 30, 2031. I read these values from PJM's own full queue export, downloaded on October 29, 2026. The interconnection.fyi page for the request at https://www.interconnection.fyi/project/pjm-c01-2036 shows the same size, fuel, county, developer and completion date. PJM's page for the request at https://www.pjm.com/m/ProjectTransition/SISReportDetails?queueNumber=C01-2036 confirms the queue number, the developer and the filing date. A grid queue entry makes the status announced. The plant is named after its county, since no other name is published. The owner is Marquis Solar LLC at 100 percent. PJM's page for the request names it as the company behind the request, and the interconnection.fyi page says the project is owned by it. Both pages were checked again on October 30, 2026. GEM accepts a project company as the owner. No parent company is named in any public document found so far. Marquis Solar LLC is not in GEM's company list, so it is a new company record. The size and fuel come from a queue tracker site, not PJM's own page, so they are less certain until PJM posts a study report. The company name sounds like a solar developer, but the queue lists the fuel as natural gas. Not found: a news story, permit, site address or turbine type. The location is approximate. No document gives the plant's own site. The point is the Marquis industrial complex at 11953 Prairie Industrial Parkway in Hennepin, Putnam County, at 41.27622, -89.31781: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=41.27622,-89.31781. The coordinates come from the EPA greenhouse gas reporting record for the Marquis ethanol plant there. The complex is the only large industrial site in Putnam County tied to the Marquis name, and the state economic development site sheet says it has 138 kilovolt power and spare gas supply. No document links Marquis Solar LLC to the Marquis companies, so this is a guess from the name. Move the point if a permit or study report names the site. Checked for duplicates on October 30, 2026. No GEM gas plant matches. Two things make this request doubtful. First, Marquis Solar LLC filed a second request the same day, C01-1722, for 120 MW of solar at the same Crescent Ridge to Corbin 138 kV line. Second, 1,150 MW is far more than a 138 kV line usually carries. The gas request may be a data entry error in PJM's queue, or a mislabeled copy of the solar request. The retired Hennepin coal plant in GEM is about half a kilometer from the center of this area, but nothing ties this request to that site.

records.researcher_notes: The Tilton Energy Center is an operating 188 MW gas peaking plant at 80 West First Street in Tilton, Vermilion County, Illinois, that is missing from GEM. The EIA-860M table for September 2026 lists it as plant 7760, Tilton Energy LLC, with four 47 MW natural gas turbines in service since June 1999. The Illinois EPA Clean Air Act permit 00050017, issued April 30, 2019 and revised February 15, 2022, names Tilton Energy, LLC as the source and lists four 47 MW natural gas combustion turbines built in May and June 1999 with water injection. An October 2011 stack test report filed with the Illinois EPA says the four turbines are identical General Electric LM-6000 simple cycle machines. Aeroderivative turbines installed together are one GEM unit, so the four turbines are entered as one unit with four engines of 47 MW each, 188 MW in total. Published totals vary: Dynegy's 2000 filing with the Securities and Exchange Commission says 176 MW, Rockland Capital's July 2017 sale release says 180 MW, and POWER Magazine's September 2022 article says 184 MW. The nameplate figure of 47 MW per turbine from the permit and the EIA table is used. History: Illinois Power leased the turbines in 1999 and subleased them to Dynegy Midwest Generation, Dynegy bought them in 2004, Rockland Capital acquired the plant in 2014 or 2015 and sold it in July 2017 to a Carlyle Group fund, and Earthrise Energy bought it from Rockland Capital in February 2022, according to POWER Magazine. The owner is Tilton Energy LLC at 100 percent. It is not in GEM's company list, so it is a new company record. Earthrise Energy is already in GEM's company list as entity 100000002885 and is the parent. The operator is not filled in. The only page naming an operator is the company's own website, which is a lead and not a citation. The location is exact. The EIA-860M point, 40.10612, -87.65382, lands on the four turbine packages beside the switchyard in satellite imagery: https://www.google.com/maps/search/?api=1&query=40.10612,-87.65382. Checked for duplicates on October 30, 2026 against the full GEM export by name, by county and by distance. No GEM plant matches. Not found: a published retirement plan, a current capacity market or interconnection filing, and a document naming the operator.
